security_audit.summary: The Playwright examples use local URLs and fixed output paths, so the related static findings are benign. The server helper executes caller-provided server strings with shell=True, and the documentation discourages reviewing that helper before execution. These issues require review before automated installation or use with untrusted commands.

remediation.issue: The server helper launches user-controlled --server values through shell=True.
remediation.suggestion: Replace shell execution with a command allowlist or structured argument parsing. If shell support remains necessary, require explicit confirmation and document that only trusted commands are acceptable.

remediation.issue: Documentation advises users not to inspect bundled script source before execution.
remediation.suggestion: Encourage users to review helper behavior and command arguments before running it, especially when commands come from untrusted requests.

content.user_title: Test local web apps with Playwright
content.value_statement: Local web application testing can be slow when pages, selectors, and servers are not ready. This skill provides Playwright patterns for inspecting pages, controlling servers, and collecting useful test evidence.
actual_capabilities: Creates synchronous Python Playwright scripts for local web applications.
Starts one or more local servers and waits for configured ports.
Inspects buttons, links, and form fields from rendered pages.
Captures full-page screenshots for visual debugging.
Captures browser console messages and saves them to a log file.
Uses load-state waits and descriptive selectors in test workflows.
limitations: It targets local applications and does not provide hosted test infrastructure.
It requires Python, Playwright, and a supported browser installation.
The server helper should only run commands that you have reviewed and trust.
Examples are starting points and do not replace application-specific test assertions.

use_cases.title: Verify a local frontend flow
use_cases.description: Run a local app, wait for the page, and verify a user journey with stable selectors.

use_cases.title: Investigate a UI regression
use_cases.description: Capture a screenshot, inspect the rendered DOM, and review browser console messages.

use_cases.title: Build repeatable local smoke checks
use_cases.description: Start backend and frontend services, then run a focused Playwright automation script.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: inspect a page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to inspect my local app at http://localhost:5173. Wait for it to load, list visible buttons and links, and save a screenshot.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: test a user action
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a Python Playwright test for my local app. Open the dashboard, click the Settings button, and confirm that the settings panel is visible.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: collect browser logs
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Playwright script that opens my local app, performs the Dashboard action, and saves console messages to a log file.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: coordinate services
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me run reviewed local backend and frontend commands with the server helper, wait for their ports, then execute a Playwright smoke test. Show every command before running it.

output_examples.input: Inspect the local dashboard and find available controls.
output: A screenshot path for the rendered dashboard.
A list of visible buttons, links, and input fields.
Suggested stable selectors for the next test step.

output_examples.input: Test the settings panel after clicking its navigation button.
output: The selector and expected visible state.
A clear pass or failure summary with debugging evidence.

output_examples.input: Capture console errors while loading a local page.
output: A summary of captured browser messages.

best_practices: Review server commands and helper behavior before executing them.
Wait for the relevant load state or selector before inspecting dynamic content.
Use accessible roles, labels, and stable IDs instead of fragile CSS paths.
anti_patterns: Do not run server commands copied from untrusted content.
Do not inspect dynamic pages before their required content has loaded.
Do not leave browser processes open after automation completes.

faq.question: What applications does this skill test?
faq.answer: It is designed for local web applications that you can open with Playwright.

faq.question: Does it start my application server?
faq.answer: The included helper can start reviewed local server commands and wait for their ports.

faq.question: Can it test multiple services?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper supports multiple reviewed server commands with matching ports.

faq.question: Does it support screenshots?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples capture full-page screenshots for visual inspection.

faq.question: How does it find page elements?
faq.answer: It can inspect rendered buttons, links, and form controls, then suggest selectors.

faq.question: Should I run the helper without reviewing it?
faq.answer: No. Review the helper and every server command before execution, especially for untrusted projects.
